firstMessage:
`checkRefundLimit` now throws the new `InvalidRefundAmountError` for a zero or negative amount. Amounts above what is left on the charge still throw `RefundTooLargeError`. The full suite passes: 37 tests, up from 36 because I added one.

Changes in `src/refunds.ts`:
- Added and exported `InvalidRefundAmountError`, which follows the existing error classes' pattern.
- Split the check: `amount <= 0` throws the new error, and `amount > leftOnCharge` throws `RefundTooLargeError`.

Changes in `src/refunds.test.ts`:
- The zero-amount assertion moved out of the "rejects more than is left" test, and it now expects the new error.
- Added a test that covers zero and a negative amount.

The `Refunder.refund` path is unchanged, so a zero or negative refund reaching it now surfaces the new error. Nothing else in `src` referenced the old behavior.

R-REFUND-LIMIT says a refund "must not exceed what is left of the original charge". It says nothing about zero or negative amounts, so the requirement text needs no update. I did not commit the change.
finalMessage:
I committed the change on a new branch, `refund-zero-amount-error`, as commit `a273e15`. I read "go ahead" as a request to commit, and I did not push or open a PR. The branch was created because `main` is the default branch.

The commit covers `src/refunds.ts` and `src/refunds.test.ts`. The suite passes with 37 of 37 tests. The working tree is clean.
